prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 街道便民服务中心一窗受理事项办理台账 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 3 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "序号" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 31px
  col 2: header "状态" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 46px
  col 3: header "内容" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 1932px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A 街道便民服务中心 ledger recording each accepted service item by serial number, processing status, and a narrative description of the case.","reading":"Readers scan the 序号 and 状态 columns first to identify and triage rows, then read the 内容 column as the substantive record; comparison is mostly across statuses and case narratives, not numeric columns.","groups":["序号 and 状态 form a compact row-identification/meta pair and belong together visually.","内容 is the substantive narrative column and should receive the remaining width."],"keep_intact":["序号 header and serial digits","状态 header and status labels such as 已办结, 办理中, 已退回, 待补正","dates, amounts, permit numbers, names, and other identifiers inside 内容"],"may_wrap":["long 内容 narratives at Chinese character or punctuation boundaries","状态 labels only in a deliberately compressed design","序号 or 状态 headers only if a compact metadata rail is chosen"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[52,67,240],"idea":"Keep 序号 and 状态 on one line at their measured minimums and give every remaining pixel to the narrative 内容 column."},{"name":"B","widths":[64,84,211],"idea":"Widen the two meta columns into a calmer, easier-to-scan identification rail, accepting a narrower and taller 内容 column."},{"name":"C","widths":[52,52,255],"idea":"Keep 序号 intact but compress 状态 into a narrow badge column that wraps inside the already tall rows, maximizing 内容 width."}]}
